name: Plastic food storage containers
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
cross_reference: Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products) governs any article in this row that is marketed for ages 0-5; the taxonomy boundary rule routes infant bottles, nipples and toddler drinkware there even though they are food-contact items.
native_basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food), Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention
native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
scope_note: Repeat-use plastic articles consisting exclusively of plastics, directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011. Because these are repeat-use articles the migration convention is the third successive migration, which is the value that governs; a first-migration result overstates compliance and is not accepted. Microwave and freezer claims extend the contact conditions and must be tested at the claimed extremes.
material: Repeat-use polypropylene, Tritan copolyester, polycarbonate or HDPE bodies, frequently with a separate lid and a silicone or thermoplastic-elastomer seal.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) container body interior; (2) lid food-contact face; (3) silicone or elastomer sealing ring, which sits outside Reg (EU) 10/2011 by its Art. 2(2)(c) exclusion of silicones and takes these ceilings by disclosed read-across; (4) any vent or valve component; (5) printed measurement graduations on an interior surface; (6) recycled-content resin streams as their own lot.
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Pb.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: lead not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
Pb.substantiation: Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell.

Cd.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cd.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: cadmium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.002 mg/kg food
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list; the published ceiling is the 0.002 mg/kg food detection limit, the strictest element value in the instrument. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. The EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium restrictions on plastics, paints and recovered PVC are percent-by-weight content restrictions and are not read into this migration cell.

tAs.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tAs.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: arsenic (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tAs.substantiation: Arsenic is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list and the instrument states it as the total element, so this cell is total arsenic and cannot be satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

iAs.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
iAs.reference_method: iAs speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

tHg.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
tHg.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: mercury (total element) not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
tHg.substantiation: Mercury is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, stated as the total element. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

MeHg.rationale: MeHg carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tHg (MeHg <= tHg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

Ni.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Ni.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: nickel specific migration limit 0.02 mg/kg food
Ni.substantiation: Nickel carries a positive specific migration limit of 0.02 mg/kg food, the tightest positive SML in the Annex II element list. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface only; where a food-contact component of the article is a nickel-bearing alloy, that component sits in the alloy-release control regime described in this row's component plan, because the plastics SML was not written for and is not achievable by a bare stainless-steel surface.

Sn.basis: organotin (dioctyltin/DOT) content as tin in skin-contact article; source unit percent by weight
Sn.source_scope: textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles, and other consumer articles in skin contact (diapers, gloves)
Sn.label: Sn 1000000 ug/kg: disclosed read-across from EU eu_reach_entry20_dot_skin_contact_articles_0_1pct (textile articles intended to come into contact w). Filled by the completeness sweep; nearest applicable sovereign for this matrix and basis.
Sn.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, register-verified (eu_reach_entry20_dot_skin_contact_articles_0_1pct). Nearest applicable sovereign Sn ceiling for this product form. Not occurrence-derived.

Al.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Al.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 1: aluminium specific migration limit 1 mg/kg food
Al.substantiation: Aluminium carries a positive specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, added by Reg (EU) 2016/1416. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number. This value governs the polymeric food-contact surface; it is not applied to an aluminium metal article, because an instrument written for plastics did not contemplate an article whose food-contact surface is the element itself.

Cr.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.label: Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: total chromium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food; the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI) is declined
Cr.substantiation: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. The body and lid consist exclusively of plastics and are within this instrument's direct scope; the silicone sealing ring is excluded from the instrument by Art. 2(2)(c) and takes the same value by disclosed read-across, which changes no number.

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total Cr (Cr-VI <= Cr), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Cr-VI speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.
